newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Singapore rubber ends steady in listless trade.
newsitem.headline: Singapore rubber ends steady in listless trade.

text.p: Rubber futures closed steady on Friday in extremely thin trade with the market seen languishing in the doldrums all of next week, dealers said.
"People are just doing some shortcovering to close off their positions before the end of the year. But the volumes involved were very slim," a rubber trader said.
"It's going to be quiet all of next week and I don't think the market will wake up from its slumber until after next week. You might as well go to sleep," another trader said.
Total volume traded reached a paltry 455 tonnes against more than 2,000 tonnes yesterday.

A string of holidays next week both here and in Japan will keep the local market quiet. The Singapore rubber futures market will be closed on January 1 for New Year and on January 2 for general elections here. In Japan, the markets will be closed on December 31 and January 1.
At around 0945 GMT, February RSS3 was seen at 125.00-126.00 U.S. cents a kg from the previous 126.00 cents.
February RSS1 was seen unchanged at 178.00 Singapore cents (US$1.27) a kg. February TSR20 was seen also unchanged at 172.25 Singapore cents (US$1.23) a kg.
